THE_PATTERN_BEING_KILLED_OFF: missing evidence -> None -> accidentally treated as acceptable. This is the same shape as the opponent_randomize ghost-field bug, where a guard read a non-existent attribute and getattr's default silently passed the very configuration it existed to reject. Absence of evidence must be a hard failure, never a default.

STANDING_RULE_EARNED_THIS_SESSION.why_it_is_not_obvious: The first instance shipped INSIDE a guardrail written specifically to prevent that class of failure, and its unit test passed because the fixture repeated the same wrong field name. A guard validated only against a fixture that mirrors its own assumption is indistinguishable from a working one.
STANDING_RULE_EARNED_THIS_SESSION.the_underlying_distinction: Runtime safety and scientific evidence are different jobs. A check can protect the run; the artifact has to prove afterward that the check actually saw what we claim it saw.
